summary: The consequence harness ran (CheckRun d5d2d6e4b4304f65ba05d1869b42fa3c, exit 0) and produced the harmful outcome the gap asked about. The node was Leader at term 2 and was deposed by an empty heartbeat one term above; the instrumented store then opened its gate, which proves a main-loop term write was in flight - the election that had read term 3, computed 4 and was held before its store. While it was held, one empty heartbeat carrying term 13 delivered on the fast path was adopted completely, with the in-memory term and the persisted term both reading 13; after the held write was released both the term and the persisted term read 5, lower than a term the node had already adopted and durably recorded, and it went on to hold leadership at that lower term. The arithmetic of this package leaves no alternative reading: a term is only ever written as the current term plus one or as an adopted higher term, so a value of 5 appearing after 13 can only come from a write computed against a stale read, which is precisely the write the gate held open and which the election continued from. That upgrades the earlier account from an unresolved invariant violation to an asserted defect with a witnessed harmful outcome, and because setCurrentTerm records the value in the stable store as well as in memory, the node keeps a durable record of a term lower than one it had already acknowledged, which is what a restart would recover. The scope I recorded is the interaction rather than either half alone: on a main-threaded path the two writes cannot interleave, and the fast path's guard keeps entries and commit-index updates out of empty heartbeats, so the exposure is the term written off the main thread while the main loop sits between its read and its write. I answered the harmful-consequence gap with this receipt and registered the cluster-level follow-up - what peers at the higher term do with a node that has gone backwards, and whether the durable inconsistency matters across a restart - as a prediction from the vote and append paths rather than something this single-node run shows. Counterweights and limits are recorded, including that the harness widened an existing window rather than inventing one, that the wrapper mirrors rather than exercises the network transport, and that one execution establishes the ordering is possible and harmful, not how likely it is. The other witnessed findings remain recorded and unaffected.
